metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Qatar

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Qatar using OECD’s PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically applies sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for each participating country/economy. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name(s) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used for variance estimation; therefore, the precise weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the provided text. For interpretation, the reported differences and confidence intervals should be understood as accounting for PISA’s complex survey design, even though the specific technical weight identifiers are not shown in this excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country factsheet summarizing descriptive and comparative PISA 2022 creative thinking results (means, proficiency levels, correlations, and relative success by ideation processes and domain contexts). It does not report an analysis pipeline that uses PV-based achievement modeling at the student level within this excerpt, so PV handling is not applicable to the extraction. Missing-data handling is not described because the factsheet focuses on published OECD estimates rather than detailing the estimation procedure for missing responses or PV generation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic subset reported for Qatar includes 15-year-old students who completed the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment as part of the PISA 2022 cycle. The factsheet states that, in Qatar, 7,676 students in 229 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 18,300 15-year-olds (an estimated 94% of the total population of 15-year-olds). No additional inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., item nonresponse thresholds, missing background questionnaire exclusions, or specific creative-thinking task completion criteria) are provided in the excerpt.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes Qatar’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-olds. The creative thinking assessment contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving). For Qatar, the mean creative thinking score is 28 on a 60-point scale, which is significantly below the OECD average (33). Qatar’s relative performance is above what would be expected from mathematics and reading performance, with 33% of the variation in creative thinking uniquely attributed to mathematics performance and correlations of 0.72 (creative thinking vs mathematics) and 0.70 (creative thinking vs reading). The factsheet also reports proficiency distributions (59% at Level 3 or above; 20% at Level 5 or 6) and within-Qatar gaps by socio-economic status and gender, plus associations between creative thinking and students’ beliefs/attitudes and school pedagogies.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. The excerpt does not describe any student-level predictive modeling, algorithmic training, or target-variable prediction; it reports published PISA estimates and descriptive comparisons. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally empty, and the extraction focuses on assessment design and reported performance benchmarks.
